caption:
Ramp data shows AI token volumes rising while spending flatlined. According to the report, token spend grew only 1.5% across August and September, after growing 42% in July. Price cuts and more cost-aware customers are part of the explanation.

In practice, this suggests companies are getting better at controlling what AI costs. What I see is that many still struggle to say what AI delivers. Usage gets counted. Value often does not.

I lived this with AskMoses.AI, the SaaS I built end to end and run as a contractor. 17 organizations in the US signed up and 6 actually use it. 11 of 17 never activated, because onboarding required a CRM and a rubric before delivering any value.

Launching is not the same as being used. Track adoption and results per use case before you scale the budget.

Comment ADOPTION and I'll DM you how I did it.
